name: move_nested_rect_is_1to1
doc: T1/§3.1 Theseus. Move one rect nested two levels deep. Speaks to the rect's own geometry only; every id in the document survives, and both containers (lyr_main, grp_inner) are bystanders that must come back byte-identical.

name: delete_bystander_leaf_keeps_containers
doc: §3.7 / T4. Deleting one leaf ends exactly one identity. The two containers are rebuilt to reach the target — the bystander clause says they must survive the rebuild unchanged.

name: boolean_union_merges_two_rects
doc: §3.3 / §3.6 UNION row. N→1: both operand identities die and the result mints a fresh id. Neither operand's id may ride out on the result — 'the frontmost source keeps the id' is the rejected rule, and over-preservation is as much a violation as under-preservation.

name: wrap_two_rects_in_group
doc: §3.4 WRAP / T5. The arrow counts material at stake: 0→1 for the new container, 1→1 for each child. Every child id survives; the wrapper's id is the one supplied by the op, and must not duplicate an existing one.

name: unpack_inner_group
doc: §3.4 UNWRAP / T5. The container's identity ends; the children keep theirs (both ports' apply_unpack_group_at already say 'children keep their ids — NO minting'). The outer layer is a bystander it must rebuild to reach the group.
